script: Spread and total were not saved for BAL@DAL, so this script is form-only. Baltimore's identity is the ground game: Derrick Henry 212 yards on 40 carries (5.3 YPC) and Lamar Jackson 77 on 8, against a Dallas defense allowing 5.33 YPC and 8 runs of 10+. Dallas has been pass-led — CeeDee Lamb 17 targets/197 yards, George Pickens 14 targets but only 68 yards — while Javonte Williams is stuck at 71 yards on 24 carries (2.96 YPC) into a Baltimore front allowing 3.62 YPC. Inferred lean: Baltimore stays on Henry and Jackson; Dallas needs Lamb through the air because the Cowboys run isn't moving the chains.
who_goes_off: Derrick Henry of Baltimore should go off against Dallas. He already has 40 carries and 212 yards over two games, and the Cowboys have allowed 5.33 yards per carry plus 8 runs of 10+. Lamar Jackson (77 rush yards on 8 carries, 9.6 YPC) is the explosive complement, not a carry thief. Mark Andrews (13 targets, 98 yards, 91 air yards) is Baltimore's underneath piece if Dallas loads the box, not the primary.
weak_spot: Dallas' real hole versus Baltimore is the run front, not the perimeter: Cowboys allow 5.33 YPC and 8 gains of 10+, with only 3 passes of 20+ on 66 attempts, so Zay Flowers' 150 yards on 6 targets is the fragile piece. Dallas pass YPA allowed is fairly flat — left 6.64 (28 att), middle 7.18 (11 att), right 6.88 (25 att) — middle is a small-sample nick, not a zone tell. Baltimore's soft spot versus Dallas is the middle: Ravens allow 9.28 YPA on 18 attempts versus 6.21 left (24 att) and 4.43 right (23 att), which is the Jake Ferguson/slot area, not outside corners on George Pickens.
injury_fallout: No injuries were saved for BAL@DAL, so nothing to reprice from a report. Usage already settles the roles: Baltimore's Henry has 40 carries versus Justice Hill's 8 carries/24 yards and Jackson's 8/77; Dallas is Javonte Williams 24/71 with Emanuel Demercado 5/15 and Hunter Luepke 2/8, not a committee that suddenly feeds Demercado's 7.5 rush line.
qb_vs_blitz: Baltimore's Lamar Jackson is fine either way — 0.22 EPA/dropback vs blitz (n=25) and 0.28 with no blitz — and Dallas blitzes only 27%, so most of his dropbacks land in the better no-blitz bucket and the Henry run stays on schedule. Dallas' Dak Prescott is the mismatch: 0.19 EPA vs blitz (n=23) versus 0.48 with no blitz, and Baltimore blitzes 32%. That Ravens blitz rate is what can knock the Cowboys off the 0.48 clean-pocket script and keep Williams from a late yardage spike.

picks.why: Baltimore's Derrick Henry is at a 106-yard pace (212 on 40 carries over weeks 1-2) against a 92.5 line, and Dallas allows 5.33 YPC with 8 runs of 10+. At a 20-carry rate even a step down to the Cowboys' 5.33 YPC allowed is about 107 yards; 18 carries at that rate is still 96, clearing 92.5 without needing his 38 receiving yards.

Dallas' Javonte Williams has 71 rush yards on 24 carries (35.5 per game, 2.96 YPC) versus a 56.5 line, into a Baltimore defense allowing 3.62 YPC and only 6 runs of 10+. Twelve carries times 3.62 is about 43 yards. He needs a carry spike well past 24-in-two-games or a YPC jump above both his 2.96 and the Ravens' 3.62 to clear 56.5, and Dak's 0.19 EPA vs a 32% Baltimore blitz does not set up a downhill Cowboys rush script.
